source.title: Evaluating Open-Source Sparse Autoencoders on Disentangling Factual Knowledge in GPT-2 Small

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether SAE features mediate factual knowledge in GPT-2 Small and reports that most tested SAE feature spaces underperform neurons, while SAE reconstructions can degrade the model's knowledge. This refines the scope of claims about SAE features as useful model units; it does not test toy-model superposition directly.
record.gate_note: The study tests SAE feature mediation and reconstruction on city-country and city-continent knowledge. It does not test feature sparsity, a superposition transition, feature importance, or whether extra features are dropped. Literature claims about polysemanticity are background, not results here. Detailed reported results are for layers 1 and 5; the paper also describes broader layer trends, including approximate scores, in Figure 1a.
record.test_reason: The study tests whether SAE features in GPT-2 Small separately mediate country and continent knowledge, compared with a neuron baseline and a DAS skyline. It also measures how much SAE reconstruction degrades that knowledge. These results bear directly on V5, and on V4's claim that SAEs recover the model's sparse features. No toy model or capacity mechanism is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that no SAE beats neurons as a feature space for separating the two facts: only the Open AI top-k SAE matches neurons, and none approaches DAS. Using SAE reconstructions always degrades city knowledge, more at layer 1 and for the Bloom and Apollo SAEs. The DAS-neuron gap is taken to show polysemantic neurons and room for better SAEs.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses RAVEL interchange interventions and differential binary masking to evaluate SAE features in GPT-2 Small; it is not a toy-model superposition experiment and does not reproduce the original method.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on layer and SAE choice. The paper reports substantial reconstruction differences between layers 1 and 5 and between SAE variants.
record.problems: One model and two factual attributes are tested; the data are filtered to 40 cities, with i.i.d. train/validation/test splits. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Results for detailed comparisons are shown for layers 1 and 5, and the authors describe the broader layer results as limited.
record.rows_left_out: The paper includes further reconstruction-loss values and sparsity statistics in Figures 1b-1c and Tables 1-2; these were left out because the rows above capture the reported feature-mediation and reconstructed-knowledge outcomes relevant to the tested versions. Figure 1a also gives broader layer trends, but its plot values are not individually transcribed here.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy model, sparsity transition or geometry.
All of it: no test of capacity competition or feature importance.
All of it: no test of what causes polysemanticity.
Other models and other attributes; feature spread beyond the country/continent subspaces.
Stability across SAE training runs or sizes, canonicality, and attributes beyond country and continent.
All of it: the dimensionality of features is not tested.

missing.what: Neuron baseline vs DAS skyline disentangle scores (71-73 vs 94-96), which the authors read as evidence of polysemantic, distributed neurons. These appear only as baselines, not as their own rows.
missing.locator: Figure 1b-1c; Section 4.2 'significant gap between baseline and skyline'

missing.what: Reconstructed knowledge accuracy across all layers (e.g. Bloom at layer 10 falls to 0.23 country and 0.03 continent).
Cross-layer disentangle scores showing that the Apollo and Bloom SAEs fall below neurons at all layers and Open AI only matches them. Read from the plot; exact values not given.

record.verdict_notes: Single model, 40 cities, one fact pair, no uncertainty estimates, and the SAEs are given i.i.d. splits to favour them. Fig 1c column headers are garbled, so the e2e vs e2e+ds attribution at layer 5 is uncertain. Table 2's Apollo rows appear offset by layer index. Several layer-5 continent reconstruction losses duplicate the layer-1 values, suggesting a transcription error in the paper. Labelling Bloom and Apollo rows 'absent' relies on scores near the ~50 a null intervention would get; the empty-intervention baseline is only plotted.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, overcomplete sparse features, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometric arrangements are not tested.
The study does not test whether capacity competition causes polysemanticity or whether feature importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
The study does not test whether polysemanticity arises for reasons other than capacity pressure.
The study tests SAE recovery of two factual attributes in GPT-2 Small, not feature spread across many neurons generally, other models, or broader LLM feature distributions.

The study evaluates SAE feature mediation and reconstruction fidelity for two attributes in GPT-2 Small. It does not test feature stability across runs or whether SAE features are canonical units generally.
The study does not determine whether underlying features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional features.
